findings.summary: The scenario's seeded workload was mostly consumed before this session: 12 decisions were already answered with undo windows closed, and no design-approval or stale-brief card ever appeared anywhere in the product (Deck, Inbox, Projects, Library). The Deck's empty state advertises 'a design to approve, a brief that went stale' as card kinds, but a user in this state can never exercise those flows, and the batch flow (10+ waiting) is unreachable — demo data reload only re-seeds a single decision.

The 10-second undo window is tight in practice: on my first genuine attempt the toast expired before the Undo click landed, and the answer was irrevocably committed. A user who hesitates even briefly loses the take-back with no recourse.

Answering the spot-check verdict commits immediately with no undo toast and no entry in the Deck's 'Answered' history — unlike decisions, there is no visible take-back window for a verdict spot-check, even though the page copy says 'Each answer can be taken back for 10 seconds'.

'Load demo data' in Settings gives no visible confirmation and applies with a noticeable delay — the Deck updated only after tens of seconds, mid-interaction, which changed the front card while I was clicking it and made two clicks land on nothing.
